title: Continuous archiving of the write-ahead log: the backup that never ends

videos.script: Every backup so far has been one moment. Whatever happened after it was lost. {{moment}} But the server already keeps a record of every change, before it makes it. It is the write-ahead log, and it lives on disk as files of sixteen megabytes. {{segments}} In this lesson you keep those files. Each one is copied away as soon as it is finished. {{archive}} Then you break the copy, and watch what the server does. It keeps every file it could not hand over, and the pile grows. {{pileup}} Left long enough, that pile fills the disk and stops the database. {{outage}} A quiet server has the opposite problem. A file can take days to fill, and the changes in it wait on one disk. {{quiet}} You fix that with a timeout, and then with a client that receives the log as it is written. {{stream}} A base backup, plus this archive, is the database at any moment you like.
